item.title: Mac lookalikes multiply as Linux raids Apple's wardrobe
item.description: Linux can do many things, but good looks aren't always its strong point. Apple has rather more of a reputation in that department, and a crop of new projects is bringing Mac-style polish to the open source desktop. Some are all-new, such as the Argentinian Lord OS , a whole new GUI desktop on top of Debian. Another, Cutefish , is a revival of a pre-ChatGPT project that never got as far as a complete release. Now it has version 1.0 for both x86-64 and Arm64, plus it's working on Mac binary compatibility via a work-in-progress layer called Reef . Ukrainian Desert OS is already at version 5.5 – practically a venerable elder in this company, despite appearing to be only about a year old. Meanwhile, ClokeOS uses Xfce for its desktop, but underneath, the OS is based on Apple's FOSS XNU kernel. The project lead plans to offer compatibility with multiple types of binaries: Linux apps, plus Mac apps via Darling , and Windows apps via Wine. This isn't new. Much as Cutefish has been revived, last year we reported on PearOS Linux , a very Mac-like skin on KDE Plasma. It has hooks in place for ambitious future features, such as Siri-style speech recognition. What's striking is the number of projects appearing and the pace of their development. Some offer both x86-64 and Arm64 builds, with Raspberry Pi editions in certain cases. For human coders, this would be months of hard work, but if it's just checking an additional box in an LLM development tool, then why wouldn't you? It's almost no extra work, but it widens the potential audience. Coveting Mac-like good looks is a longstanding urge among Linux users, and with legitimate reason. There's nothing wrong with Macs, even if you are mainly a FOSS user. Modern macOS, or OS X as it was called a decade ago, is a Unix underneath its shiny proprietary desktop, and many of the flagship Linux FOSS apps also have Mac versions, from Firefox and Thunderbird, via LibreOffice, to VirtualBox, plus less well-known but very handy apps such as Ferdium and Panwriter. We've written about the usefulness of FOSS apps on macOS before, including for reviving elderly Macs . Just a couple of months ago, we published a two-part guide on how to give Xfce a macOS-like layout and then how to tweak it so apps fit in better . We focused on the functionality, though, not the looks – we don't really care much for such things. If it does matter to you, though, you're not alone, and there are lots of themes and skins to make Xfce look prettier. Some of these are all-in-one packages that you can install on an existing distro to give it a new look. One recent example is Cupertino , developed with assistance from Claude. From a few years ago, there are Small Sur and Ventura-Xfce . From nine years ago, long pre-LLM, there is osXFCE . We can see the appeal. item.title: Oak Ridge labs gets hybrid quantum-HPC system to test qubit error correction
item.description: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) now boasts a system for research into quantum error correction, combining IBM quantum processors with a high-performance compute (HPC) system based on AMD silicon. The Quantum Science Center ( QSC ) at ORNL, funded by the US Department of Energy (DoE), unveiled what it calls a co-design platform for quantum error correction, marrying up quantum and HPC technology. While useful, fault-tolerant quantum systems always seem to be at least a decade away, there have been notable advances over the past several years in the field of quantum error correction, according to ORNL. These include early demonstrations of protecting quantum information from environmental noise, which can cause loss of the fragile quantum states needed for computations. "Solving the challenges of quantum error correction is essential to making quantum computing a practical tool for scientific discovery, which is a priority for Oak Ridge National Laboratory," said QSC director Travis Humble. IBM Fellow and director of IBM Research Jay Gambetta said that it was no longer a question of whether error correction works, but how to accelerate and optimize error correction to build systems that scientists can use to tackle challenging problems. "This new co-design platform for quantum error correction allows us to evaluate different approaches and determine the architectures, software and workflows that will scale," he stated. ORNL's new tool combines an IBM Quantum System Two, equipped with the latest 120-qubit Nighthawk r2 quantum processors , and Umbra, a classical HPC system powered by AMD 5th Gen Epyc CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPU accelerators. According to AMD, the CPUs provide the orchestration and general-purpose performance needed to coordinate everything, while the GPUs accelerate simulation, optimization and the parallel scientific computations surrounding quantum workloads. Also part of the system are AMD Versal SoCs to provide the low-latency control, readout and decoding capabilities for the quantum circuitry. ORNL says that this brings together the computing infrastructure needed for quantum error correction in a single environment, and opens it up to more researchers than ever before. They will use it to develop and validate quantum algorithms, workflows, and applications in an environment built for quantum-centric supercomputing, an emerging paradigm where quantum processors (QPUs), CPUs, and GPUs work together as one system. IBM says that one promising approach the co-design platform cloud explore is hierarchical error correction. It describes this as using an inner code to protect qubits within a module, while an outer code wraps around the inner code’s logical qubits and adds a second layer of protection. This approach could reach a trillion logical operations at a physical error rate of one in a thousand, IBM research suggested. These hierarchical codes rely on having powerful classical compute, and the co-design platform will give

item.title: Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced . Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation. The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger. From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations. How the FBI credentials turned into cash Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said. FOX 5 DC , citing the same U.S. Attorney’s Office release , noted the Portugal planning that appears in the plea papers. Yaroch asked ChatGPT how to maximize investment returns and where to live in the European Union. After the chatbot suggested buying a vineyard in Portugal, he gave Portuguese lawyers a power of attorney on June 15, 2026, to register him with the Portuguese Tax and Customs Authority, obtain a tax identification number and collect the password to his finance portal. He arranged travel to Portugal for September 2026. What the plea says the FBI lost The agreed statement of facts goes beyond the dollar figure. Yaroch’s conduct compromised multiple FBI investigations into criminal groups and nation-state adversaries, the office said, and it compromised FBI sources and methods used in fo

item.title: Giant exoplanet emerges from the dark when the James Webb Space Telescope turns out the starlight
item.description: null Sometimes science can seem really counter-intuitive. For example, occasionally in astronomy, you can see more with less light. Case in point: the emergence of a giant planet in observations made by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), when astronomers found a way to block out light from the planet's parent star. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , in question is 51 Eridani b (51 ERI b), a gas giant with the same mass as around 11 Jupiters that orbits a star located around 97 light-years away. 51 ERI b was discovered back in 2015 by ground-based telescopes, but the planet was missing from observations of the system made by the JWST. That wasn't a failing of the JWST itself; no one is doubting the observing capabilities of the most powerful telescope humanity has ever hoisted into orbit around Earth. Instead, it was a result of starlight from the star 51 ERI A obscuring this intimidatingly massive world. The brightest planets are 100,000 times fainter than their host stars, meaning spotting them is like observing a firefly hovering around a lighthouse. Even using a tool called a coronagraph to block the star isn't enough to reveal the planet, as that doesn't stop all the starlight. The only solution to this glaring problem is a computer program to wipe out the starlight. "For the past 20 years, astronomers have tackled this problem by observing a different star and using its image as a reference," Jason Wang of Northwestern University explained in a statement . "Then, they subtract that reference image from the original observation to remove the unwanted glare to reveal faint planets that otherwise might be hidden." There is a problem with this process, however. Even the most stable telescopes "wobble." For instance, the JWST requires cryocoolers to keep its NIRCam instrument super cold, and those coolers have little motors that can cause the mirrors to vibrate. This movement, however slight, causes a scatter in starlight. The result is enough glare remaining to obscure a planet, but Wang and colleagues developed a new approach to this problem. Telescopes their more stable digital twins The new approach taken by the team is dubbed Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), and it involves creating a digital "twin" of a telescope. Essentially a virtual replica that simulates how starlight travels through the telescope's mirrors and reaches its detectors. This twin is then fine-tuned to account for millions of tiny imperfections in the original telescope. The digital twin is then tweaked until it aligns with observations from the actual telescope. Astronomers can then remove the simulated glare from the original image. To assess the validity of the technique, the researchers took a second look at JWST observations of two star systems with known exoplanets, HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani , and one system, TYC 5899, with no known planets. The researchers found that, in terms of detecting faint exoplanets, FLIP outperformed conventional image

On Oct. 21, the publisher announced that it was closing BioWare , the beloved studio behind games like Mass Effect , Dragon Age, and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic . The news came just a few months after EA was purchased by the Saudi Arabian government’s Public Investment Fund, Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners, and private equity firm Silver Lake. Despite these dismal circumstances, including the fact that EA is now owned by a government responsible for numerous human rights abuses , a small group of EA developers just finished an unexpected feel-good preservation project.

item.title: Giants Urged to Consider Trade for RB Not Named Jonathan Taylor
item.description: As the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches on November 10, the New York Giants have become one of the most active buyers on the market. Joe Schoen and company have been heavily involved in trade rumors with the deadline just days away. So far this season, the Giants have been the best team in the NFC East. Even after the season-ending injuries to quarterback Jaxson Dart and pass rusher Brian Burns, the team has continued finding ways to win football games. One of the main interests for New York in trade discussions has reportedly been upgrading the running back position. The team has been linked to multiple star running backs, including Indianapolis Colts superstar Jonathan Taylor. Saquon Barkley has been another name thrown around, as has Derrick Henry. While the flashy trade for a proven superstar would be very interesting, the Giants have other options as well. Jun 9, 2026; East Rutherford, NJ, USA; New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh answers questions from the press after the minicamp activities at Quest Diagnostics Center. Mandatory Credit: Thomas Salus-Imagn Images Giants Urged to Consider Trade for Non-Superstar Running Back Matt Levine of Giants Roundtable has suggested that Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard could be a great fit for New York. “Skattebo hasn’t been awful for the team, but his lack of ball security at times has cost the Giants. But mixing his power running with the speed and patience of Pollard could help the Giants become a well-balanced running team,” Levine wrote . “It remains unknown how the Giants will approach the trade deadline next week, but this team does want to get into the playoffs. And going after an update at running back could be one way for them to make it happen.” Pollard may not be a superstar, but he has played very good football this season. In eight games played, the 29-year-old running back has carried the football 133 times for 595 yards and six touchdowns, averaging 4.5 yards per attempt. He has also caught 14 passes for 70 yards. Making a move for Pollard would be much cheaper than a trade for Taylor, Henry, or Barkley. He would still provide a boost at the running back position, but he wouldn’t cost the Giants nearly as much draft capital. Only time will tell what New York choose to do before the deadline. However, the running back position seems to be a primary target and Pollard is a name worth monitoring. item.title: Colton Herta qualifies for F1 superlicence as Valtteri Bottas remains bullish on 2027 seat
item.description: Motorsport photo Cadillac F1 test driver Colton Herta has finally obtained the last remaining superlicence point required to drive in the series, but incumbent Valtteri Bottas remains bullish on his future with the squad. Herta conducted his sixth Friday practice session of the 2026 season at Interlagos, reaching the required threshold of 100km to earn his 40th superlicence point needed to race in F1. Read Also: F1 Brazilian GP: Lando Norris tops FP1 as Colton Herta clinches superlicence Cadillac believed the former IndyCar ace had reached that threshold last week in Mexico, but it soon emerged the Californian was still one point shy amid confusion over his previous IndyCar results. The US-owned squad rectified that error by handing Herta another Friday FP1 session in Sergio Perez's car. That allows the team to keep its options open as it considers retaining incumbent Bottas for a second year alongside Perez or handing Herta his F1 debut in 2027. The amount of time, energy and money spent by Cadillac to prepare Herta and ensure he kept churning out FP1 sessions suggests that the team is set on promoting the 26-year-old American as early as next year. But Bottas was bullish on retaining his seat for 2027 and said he was bemused by the extent of the rumours around his seat after a difficult year with the troubled Cadillac MAC-26. Alongside Herta, several other drivers have either held private talks with Cadillac or publicly applied for Bottas' seat, like Mercedes reserve driver Frederik Vesti. "I've been quite surprised about the amount of noise on that," Bottas said on Thursday. "Because I know what my situation is. And all I've heard, the team has been happy with what I'm doing. Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing "But at the same time, we know how this sport works. Everyone wants to be in F1 and if somebody sees an opportunity somewhere, they're going to try and go for it one way or the other. "But the way our team is structured and the way decisions are made for the future, everything needs to be approved by the board. And I believe that meeting is still yet to happen. I've been convinced nothing has changed." Bottas has underperformed compared to team-mate Perez, but has also dealt with numerous issues with Cadillac's debut car, the latest coming in the shape of a high-speed accident in Mexico due to a suspension failure. That has made the Finnish veteran's performances tougher to judge, but the 10-time race winner insists the right people know how to appraise him. "I think the people who know, they know. That's what I feel like. And I've got good support on that side," the 37-year-old said. "We have bigger problems to solve than the drivers at the moment and I think Mexico was a good example. "The team knows what they can get out of me if everything works well. But so far, they haven't really delivered with a car that I can do much. But honestly, that was always what I kind of expected for the first year. I came

item.title: Kenny Beecham calls Warriors broadcast ‘the worst in the whole league’ after it defends Draymond Green
item.description: Credit: NBC Sports Bay Area The 2026-27 NBA season is underway, and while every NBA season brings plenty of change, it seems that some things are destined to always stay the same. The Golden State Warriors’ local NBC Sports broadcast team of Bob Fitzgerald and Kelenna Azubuike has finished in last place in Awful Announcing’s local NBA announcer rankings for three years running. Graders not only found Fitzgerald “condescending” and too focused on “teaching” the audience or complaining about referees, but the booth was also called out for its “homerism,” which even Warriors fans found excessive. That homerism reared its head again during Monday’s game between the Warriors and Phoenix Suns. Warriors forward Draymond Green was assessed a technical foul for throwing Suns center Khaman Maluach to the ground and escalating things with Suns guard Dillon Brooks afterward. However, if you let Fitzgerald and Azubuike tell it, everything Green did was within the lines. A notion so ridiculous that it wasn’t wasted on NBA content creator Kenny Beecham, who found himself on Awful Announcing’s 2026 list of rising stars in sports media. “I’m listening to this Warriors broadcast, and listen, they’ve been around for so long, this is not a new take, but I just remembered why the f*ck I don’t listen to the Warriors broadcast,” Beecham said on the Numbers On The Board podcast. Kenny speaks on the Warriors’ Broadcasters https://t.co/sWUceaucYB — Numbers On The Board (@notbpod) November 5, 2026 “It is the worst broadcast in the whole league by a wide margin, because every broadcast has to be biased. That’s why you listen to [Chicago Bulls announcer Adam Amin] and rest in peace, Stacey King. You want them to be Bulls fans, but also you don’t want them to be jack*sses while being Bulls fans. “And I feel like what they be doing in that Warriors broadcast is so jack*ssery where nobody can be wrong on the Warriors. Draymond grabbed Maluach, body-slammed him, and then choked Dillon Brooks! And it was like, ‘Well, I don’t know if they gonna get him on the choke.’ “Bro, Dillon Brooks face was purple!” Beecham and Awful Announcing’s readers are hardly alone in their assessment of Fitzgerald and Azubuike. Last year, Zach Lowe asserted that there was “no more homer broadcast in the entire NBA, and for all I know in the world of sports, than the Warriors’ broadcast.” We’re just barely past the 10% mark into the season, but it sounds like the Warriors broadcast is well on its way to its fourth consecutive last-place local announcer rankings finish. The post Kenny Beecham calls Warriors broadcast ‘the worst in the whole league’ after it defends Draymond Green appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Zach Allen and Malcom Roach Are Quietly Dominating in Denver
item.description: In a league obsessed with highlight-reel edge rushers and flashy defensive backs, the Denver Broncos have quietly built one of the NFL’s most relentless pass rushes from the inside out. Over eight weeks, the Broncos rank among the league’s top teams in sacks, and a massive share of that pressure comes from two players who almost never light up national headlines: Zach Allen and Malcolm Roach . While the spotlight stays locked on the usual suspects, these two interior defensive linemen keep collapsing pockets, generating constant chaos up the middle, and turning routine dropbacks into frantic escapes for opposing quarterbacks. Allen and Roach put up elite production, yet they remain heavily underrated. They don’t just rack up sacks and pressures. They absorb double teams, free up the edge rushers, stuff the run, and create the interior chaos that makes the Broncos defense click. Their consistency and two-way impact are a big reason Denver’s front has been so disruptive this season. Still, they fly under the national radar week after week. That needs to change. The Quiet Engine of Denver’s Front Zach Allen has spent the 2026 season doing what he does best, dominating from the interior without demanding the spotlight. Through eight weeks, the 29-year-old defensive lineman owns a 79.2 overall PFF grade (fifth among all interior defensive linemen) and leads the entire position group with 34 pressures. Those pressures have produced 4.5 official sacks, a league-high number of quarterback hits among interior players, and constant disruption that forces offenses to account for him on every snap. What makes Allen especially valuable is how he helps everyone around him. He routinely draws double teams, opening lanes for edge rushers like Nik Bonitto and creating one-on-one opportunities for Malcolm Roach. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph has publicly pushed Allen to elevate his run defense this year, and the results show: Allen’s improved strength against the run has helped solidify the entire front. Teammates notice the impact even when the national cameras don’t. As one fellow lineman put it earlier this season, Allen is “ so good at opening things up for other people.” He even made a huge special-teams play against the 49ers in Week 5, flying in to block a field-goal attempt at the end of the first half and keeping the game tied. Elite Numbers, Little Recognition The numbers only get more impressive the deeper you dig. Allen ranks first among interior defensive linemen in total pressures, sits near the top of the league in quarterback hits, and maintains an elite 82.1 PFF pass-rush grade . He has also been one of the most consistent snap-to-snap performers on the Broncos’ defense, logging a heavy workload while still producing at a high level against both the pass and the run. Few interior players in the NFL are matching this combination of volume and efficiency. Even with those numbers, the national coverage on Allen still feels surprisingly shallow.

item.title: Ducks land in CFP rankings despite rocky season
item.description: Oregon football’s season hasn’t worked out the way it expected. But the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) were ranked in the first College Football Playoff rankings. item.title: Liverpool star named in England squad for UEFA Nations League fixtures
item.description: Liverpool star named in England squad for UEFA Nations League fixtures England Squad 2026: Rio Ngumoha Included as Thomas Tuchel Turns to Youth Thomas Tuchel has named a 25-man England squad for the final Nations League fixtures of 2026, and there are a few obvious takeaways. The first is that youth is getting its chance. The second is that a few established names are still on the outside looking in. Liverpool’s sole representative is Rio Ngumoha, the 18-year-old forward who continues to hold Tuchel’s attention. He is still at the start of his senior international career, but the pattern is clear. Tuchel saw something in Florida before the World Cup and has kept him involved since. Rio Ngumoha keeps England place Ngumoha has three senior caps so far and no goals, but that barely matters at this stage. He made his debut in the 1-0 win over New Zealand in Tampa on 6 June, coming on for the second half and becoming England’s fifth-youngest debutant. His competitive debut followed in the 2-0 Nations League win over Czechia. At 18 years and 31 days, only Wayne Rooney and Jude Bellingham were younger when making a competitive debut for England. He then added another substitute appearance against the same opposition a week later. For Liverpool, it is another sign that Ngumoha is moving quickly. He is no passenger in this squad. He is there because Tuchel wants a closer look. Photo: IMAGO Thomas Tuchel calls up fresh names Jobe Bellingham and Josh King both receive their first senior call-ups. Bellingham, now at Borussia Dortmund, steps up with his reputation growing. King, the Fulham teenager, had already trained with the squad before the 2026 World Cup and now makes the full jump. Ben White returns, while Cole Palmer is left out again and has not featured for England since March. Phil Foden is also absent. Those omissions matter because these are not fringe players. Tuchel is making choices, and they are hard ones. England Nations League schedule set England close the group stage with two demanding matches. Croatia visit Wembley on Thursday 12 November, then comes a trip to Madrid to face world champions Spain on Sunday 15 November. Finish first or second and England are into the quarter-finals next March. The forward options include Harry Kane, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers, with Eberechi Eze and Morgan Gibbs-White also selected. Former Liverpool players Trent Alexander-Arnold, now with Real Madrid, and Jarell Quansah of Bayer Leverkusen are included too. The headline, though, is simple enough. Ngumoha remains in the frame.

item.title: Man United’s Big Summer Signing Set To Miss ‘Number of Weeks’
item.description: Man United’s Big Summer Signing Set To Miss ‘Number of Weeks’ Carlos Baleba Injury Blow Leaves Manchester United Facing Midfield Test Manchester United’s season has acquired an awkward complication. Carlos Baleba, the midfielder signed for £70m in the summer to lend force and mobility to the centre of Michael Carrick’s team, now appears set for a spell on the sidelines that may stretch deep into the winter. The early indication is sobering. Baleba felt his hamstring during United’s comeback win against Roma on Tuesday, pulling up at the beginning of the second half and leaving the field in visible distress. What had first seemed likely to rule him out of the weekend now threatens to remove him from a significant portion of the schedule ahead, including the visit to Anfield on 22 November and the Champions League meeting with Sporting CP three days later. Baleba Injury Disrupts Midfield Plans For Carrick, this is damaging in ways that go beyond simple availability. Baleba has only started five matches since arriving from Brighton, in part because an ankle problem delayed the beginning of his campaign. Even so, his presence has offered a glimpse of the athletic profile United believed they were buying, a midfielder capable of covering ground quickly, recovering possession and accelerating transitions through the middle third. Now that process of integration must pause again. Carrick confirmed the prognosis remains incomplete, though the broad outline is already clear. “We don’t know, but it will be a number of weeks,” said manager Michael Carrick, “It won’t be after the international break [that Baleba returns]. It’ll be a little bit longer than that.” Photo: IMAGO Michael Carrick Weighs United Options That leaves United to navigate a busy run without a player recruited to raise the ceiling of their midfield. December alone contains seven fixtures, among them a demanding trip to Arsenal on 20 December, and there is no certainty Baleba will be restored by then. Carrick must also judge how quickly he can reintroduce Patrick Dorgu. The defender has returned to partial training after hamstring trouble of his own, though the sense from United is that caution will prevail. His involvement against Aston Villa remains undecided, with the staff wary of forcing the issue after successive muscle problems. For now, United are left with an old football truth. Carefully built plans can be altered in an instant, and the cost of absence is often measured not only in matches missed, but in momentum surrendered.

item.title: Red Sox Reportedly 'Unlikely' To Re-sign Sonny Gray; What's Plan In Rotation?
item.description: Free agent pitcher Sonny Gray Sonny Gray's mutual option was declined after a tremendous season with the Boston Red Sox. Gray has decided that he wants to keep pitching, and he should have no shortage of suitors on the open market. Despite playing in his 14th season at 36 years old, he posted a 2.72 ERA and had one of the best years of his career. He is more than just a middle rotation arm, but it does not sound like the Red Sox will bring him back. "Gray was fantastic, the team’s best starter," wrote The Boston Globe's Alex Speier. "But at this stage of the offseason, it seems unlikely the Sox will bring him back via free agency given the expected return to health of Crochet and emergence of Tolle." The Red Sox should have Crochet, Tolle, Ranger Suarez and Jake Bennett in the rotation next year. They will likely be expecting Brayan Bello to return to being a quality starter like he was in 2025, and his second-half success last season should reassure them. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! It's hard to argue they will be better without Gray, but they made it through last season without their ace, essentially. They have bigger needs to address than the rotation. "While the Sox may look to add depth, they consider lineup upgrades more critical — particularly given their growing confidence in their pitching pipeline to stabilize the rotation," wrote Speier. "Of course, such a statement comes with the caveat that in the 2025-26 offseason, the Sox didn’t plan on signing Suarez, but did so once they whiffed on their top positional targets." More MLB: Nationals Will Reportedly 'Shop' CJ Abrams; Which Teams Make Sense As Suitors?

item.title: ONE Friday Fights 177 Co-Main Event Result: Superball Storms Onto The Global Stage With Liver-Shot Finish Of Saksri
item.description: Superball Sitcho made the most of his maiden opportunity to compete on the global stage, announcing himself in emphatic fashion with a first-round liver shot against Saksri Superlek Muaythai in the flyweight Muay Thai co-main event of ONE Friday Fights 177 . Live in Asia primetime from Bangkok’s Lumpinee Stadium on Friday, November 6, the all-Thai showdown was thrilling while it lasted. Despite this being his first fight in 4-ounce gloves Muay Thai, the 24-year-old promotional newcomer looked right at home, bursting out of the gates on dynamic footwork that set up a one-two and a crisp leg kick. Photo Credit: ONE Championship His finesse didn’t stop there, either. Next came a spinning side kick, with a clean elbow following right behind it. The Sitcho martial artist was clearly enjoying himself out there, and he was in no mood to make the night a long one. Saksri had other ideas, at least for a moment. He did catch a teep and answered with a left hook of his own, but that was the only significant shot he landed all night. Superball soon swarmed him with a three-punch combination upstairs, then finished the job with a liver shot to his open midsection. The fight was stopped at 1:42 of round one, with Saksri on the canvas and unable to continue. The statement victory lifted Superball to 71-30 and added another exciting name to watch in the weekly series. item.title: Tigers tweak coaching staff, bring in familiar face to front office
item.description: Detroit Tigers manager A.J. Hinch has tweaked his coaching staff, the organization has brought back a familiar face to work in the front office and the Tigers have made changes atop their medical and athletic training departments. Taken as a whole, it's clear the Tigers are trying to improve on the field for 2027 . After a rash of injuries in 2026, they are making changes to the medical side. And they have added to their baseball operations side. The Tigers named Kyle Hudson as their first base and baserunning coach on Friday, Nov. 6. Hudson, who was the Boston Red Sox third base coach, replaces Anthony Sanders. Hudson, a 39-year-old who played for Baltimore in 2011, will also help coach the outfielders. Hudson was part of Alex Cora's staff with the Red Sox and lost his job when Cora was fired in April. Our Tigers book is the perfect holiday gift The Tigers also named former longtime MLB catcher Martin Maldonado as their quality coach. This move is interesting because it could provide another benefit: Maldonado will be a friendly face for Tigers pitcher Framber Valdez – Maldonado caught him in Houston. Maldonado was behind the dish when Valdez threw a no-hitter against Cleveland on Aug. 1, 2023. And Ryan Sienko, who was the Tigers catching coach, has added duties as bullpen coach. In addition, the Tigers also announced the return of Jay Sartori to the front office as vice president of baseball operations. Sartori started in 2015 under Al Avila and then worked for Scott Harris. With the Tigers, he developed "Caesar," which became the club's internal software system in 2017. "Jay was incredible when I first got here [in October 2020],” Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said Sept. 19. "He was very instrumental in the building of a lot of different processes, a lot of different things behind the scenes, and it's never talked about publicly. It's never really you know discussed on the credit that goes around to building the infrastructure of an organization." FOR THE WIN: Meet the Tigers pitching prospect who came out of nowhere Sartori left the Tigers in August 2025 to join the Atlantic Coast Conference as vice president of sport technology and innovation, in order to be closer to family. "Obviously, it's a huge addition to come back," Hinch said back in September. "Friendly face, somebody who has a lot of deep relationships with people, my staff and the guys downstairs, but he's a tireless worker. He takes so much off the plate of other people around baseball operations. So when I when I was told he was coming back, I reached out to him and looked forward to getting him back in the mix. His impact is understated because of how it's behind the curtain and done in a non-public way, but that doesn't make it non-impactful." The Tigers also made changes to the medical side. item.title: Manchester United boss Michael Carrick provides Carlos Baleba injury update
item.description: Manchester United summer signing Carlos Baleba was forced off with an injury during their comeback win against AS Roma -Credit:Molly Darlington, Getty Images Carlos Baleba faces a multi-week absence after suffering a hamstring injury during Manchester United's comeback victory over AS Roma. The midfielder was substituted just after the half-time break in the thrilling win against the Serie A side, having pulled up clutching his hamstring following a powerful run into the penalty area. Having already missed the start of the season with an ankle problem sustained during preseason following his £70 million ($95 million) move from Brighton and Hove Albion, Baleba now faces another extended spell on the treatment table. USMNT's Nations League roster revealed as Mauricio Pochettino explains Ricardo Pepi absence Soccer star Jesús de Miguel tragically dies aged 30 after mid-game collision as tributes paid -Credit:Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images Michael Carrick confirmed the 22-year-old will not be available immediately after the international break, ruling him out of Premier League clashes against Aston Villa and Liverpool, as well as the UEFA Champions League away fixture against Sporting in Lisbon. "Carlos, we don't know exactly, but it'll be a number of weeks," said Carrick via the Manchester Evening News . "It's definitely not this week, and it won't be any time over the international break. It'll be a little bit longer than that." Carrick was also tight-lipped on whether Patrick Dorgu could return to the matchday squad for the first time since September 20, after the winger resumed training earlier this week following his own hamstring issue. It marks the second hamstring setback of the calendar year for the Denmark international, who previously missed three months after the January victory at Arsenal — Carrick's second match at the helm. "Patrick's done a little bit of training this week," said Carrick. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "As you've seen, he trained with us at the start of the week, very, very small. So we've got to be patient with Pat. "He's had a good period of time now with a couple of hamstrings that we need to manage that and be patient with that over the next few weeks as well. But he's slowly getting back with us, so we'll have to see whether he can be involved at the weekend or not."

item.title: Packers Insider Gives Team Clear Directive Before Trade Deadline
item.description: The Green Bay Packers and general manager Brian Gutekunst have been heavily involved in the NFL rumor mill leading up to the November 10 trade deadline. No one knows whether or not the team will make a big move, but the rumors have been out there that they have shown interest. Most notably, the Packers have been heavily connected to a potential blockbuster trade for Indianapolis Colts superstar running back Jonathan Taylor. They aren’t viewed as the front-runner to make that move, but they have at least had interest in swinging big. Over the years, Green Bay has not been known as an aggressive buyer at trade deadlines. Instead, the Packers have focused on drafting and developing, while adding veteran pieces around the edges. The trade Micah Parsons last year helped change some of that lack of aggressiveness. So far this season, the team has looked like a potential contender in some moments and a team who could miss the playoffs in others. They have the talent to be a Super Bowl caliber team. However, a move or two is needed. With that being said, one longtime Green Bay insider has spoken out with a clear directive for the team before the deadline. Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) takes off on a run Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, during the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Green Bay Packers Urged to Get Aggressive at NFL Trade Deadline Sports Illustrated’s Bill Huber believes that it’s time for the Packers to make a Super Bowl move. He thinks they should be open to making a blockbuster trade. “To do big things requires bold actions. The Packers’ championship drought is too long. Now is the time to stop ‘being in every conversation’ and actually make the move to perhaps bring another title to Titletown,” Huber wrote . That statement from Huber is music to the ears of the fans. Green Bay has typically opted to not make the final move that could lead to a Super Bowl winning run. Making the trade for Taylor could be the final missing piece. The Packers could also consider an aggressive move to fix the offensive line like trading with the Philadelphia Eagles for Landon Dickerson. Only time will tell what Green Bay chooses to do. But, it’s clear that Huber and much of the Packers’ fan base believes that the time is now for Gutekunst and the front office to take a home run swing. item.title: ‘Social media made y’all way too comfortable’: Sophie Cunningham shares a message after election
item.description: Aug 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) looks on during the second half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Sophie Cunningham had plenty to say on social media the day after the midterm elections. After sharing a post about “being better Americans” on Wednesday, the Indiana Fever guard followed it up with another message. This time, Cunningham shared a blunt quote from boxing legend Mike Tyson to her Instagram story, which took aim at people who feel comfortable disrespecting others online. Cunningham’s Post-Election Message On Wednesday, a day after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, Cunningham reposted a lengthy message from podcaster and entrepreneur Andy Frisella to her Instagram story. The post argued that the country’s problems can’t be fixed through elections alone. “One of the strangest things about our culture is how much faith we’ve placed in elections to change our lives and how little faith we’ve placed in our own ability to do the same,” the post read. “Politics is downstream of culture. We can keep changing the people in charge, passing new laws and arguing over which party has the answers … but until we change the culture fostering, producing and tolerating the problems we have as a society, nothing fundamentally changes,” it continued. The post didn’t mention a party or candidate. But the timing was notable, coming from a player who has become a lightning rod for her political views. Cunningham sparked a firestorm this summer when she said she wants to protect girls from having to compete against “biological men,” comments that critics called transphobic. Still, Cunningham has insisted that her political views fall right in the middle . “I’m very much in the middle. I agree with things on both sides, disagree with things on both sides,” Cunningham told ESPN’s Hallie Grossman in July. Mike Tyson Quote Later, Cunningham shared another message to her Instagram story, this time a quote from Tyson. “Social media made y’all way too comfortable with disrespecting people and not getting punched in the face for it,” the post read, according to OutKick . Cunningham did not add any comment of her own, and it’s unclear what, if anything, prompted her to share it. She has been vocal about how she’s treated online, though. Earlier this week, Cunningham called her critics “ psychotic ” and said they have “so much hatred in their heart.” She also recently revealed that she has hired 24/7 security . The post ‘Social media made y’all way too comfortable’: Sophie Cunningham shares a message after election appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Beach volleyball pro Alex Ukkelberg comes out: 'Thankful that I'm gay'
item.description: Alex Ukkelberg said he has been living his best life as an out gay man in Los Angeles for years, having come out to family, friends and in the pro beach volleyball community. But beyond that, it wasn’t until Wednesday that he said anything about it publicly. "There's no way I could be gay," the 32-year-old from tiny Battle Lake, Minnesota said in his coming out video . "Is there?" "When you grow up in a town of less than 800 people, being different is almost always a bad thing — and it’s definitely something you want to hide," Ukkelberg wrote in the caption. "I knew I was different from a young age.. but I didn’t know what that meant." “I’ve been out for a long time to family and friends and as I shared more on social media it just felt like a good thing to say. Visibility matters,” Ukkelberg told the LGBTQ+ sports site Outsports in an interview following his social media post. See on Instagram In his video, the former women's volleyball coach for the St. Cloud State Huskies talked about the various sports he played growing up: He ran track and competed in basketball, baseball, and football. Ukkelberg said while he knew he wanted to be an athlete, he said he thought that meant "there's no way I could be gay." That's the message he said the world reinforced, as he showed a flurry of images of him as both a student-athlete and as a guy dating women. Ukkelberg confessed that he actually didn't even think of himself as gay for many years. "Up until my sophomore year of college, I genuinely thought I was straight," he said, adding that he intensely felt the weight of finally admitting his identity for the first time. “Saying the words ‘I’m gay’ out loud for the first time was really hard for me,” said Ukkelberg. He added that he struggled with his sexuality so much that for a long time, he contemplated staying in the closet. But the toll of hiding who he was while pursuing sports was too much, he said. “After quite a few years of very bad mental health, I decided I wasn’t able to give up either identity. I was just going to have to figure out how to be both, and honestly, I’m thankful that I’m gay. It’s made me a better, more empathetic person,” said Ukkelberg. "I think I’ve always found it easier to let people get to know me first before I come out to them, rather than having to break through stereotypes just to be seen for who I am," he wrote in the caption to the video. "I’ve gotten it from both directions — too gay, not gay enough.. Nobody wants to be put in a box — especially not the young gay kid from a small town in rural Minnesota." Ukkelberg revealed in the video that his decision to come out publicly has taken him more than a decade to figure out, and he's still at it. “Despite being out for over 10 years, I’ve conveniently left that part of my story off social media because I’m still figuring out how to talk about it. I’ve gone back and forth on how or what to say or if I should just say nothing at all. I don’t want to say the wrong thing,

item.title: Doc Rivers throws Giannis Antetokounmpo under the bus after messy Bucks break-up
item.description: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Doc Rivers throws Giannis Antetokounmpo under the bus after messy Bucks break-up appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Bucks look like a completely different team than they did last year around this time, and it’s because Giannis Antetokounmpo is with the Miami Heat, and Doc Rivers is not the head coach. Rivers had a front-row seat to the chaos last season where it seemed like the Bucks were going to trade Antetokounmpo before the deadline, but never did. In a recent interview with Bill Simmons, Rivers shared his side of the story and believes that Antetokounmpo was “yo-yoing” the Bucks into trading him. “Giannis wanted out, but he was a Buck. And he didn’t want to be the bad guy,” Rivers said. “He wanted John [Horst] and Wes [Edens] and those guys to say, ‘we’re trading you’ instead of him asking for a trade. To me, that was the game that was being played.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Doc Rivers says Giannis Antetokounmpo wanted out of Milwaukee, but didn't want to look like the "bad guy" to protect his legacy "Giannis wanted out, but he was a Buck. And he didn't want to be the bad guy. He wanted John and Wes and those guys to say, 'we're trading you' instead… pic.twitter.com/kZB6R0ZArs — NBABase (@TheNBABase) November 6, 2026 Rivers didn’t stop there, and he continued to talk about what it was like coaching Antetokounmpo, and from his experience, it wasn’t easy. “He’s not easy. He plays at this crazy downhill pace,” Rivers said. “He’s really a difficult guy. He has this great passing ability, but he doesn’t have a super-high IQ at the same time. He really has only one way of playing. Every play, he wants to force it. I wish he’d learned how to execute better. Doc Rivers says Giannis Antetokounmpo doesn’t have a super-high IQ and that he was NOT easy to coach 😳 pic.twitter.com/aywGPNxaEW — Fullcourtpass (@Fullcourtpass) November 6, 2026 “The thing he still needs to learn is the value of execution how important it is, when you’re in practice and at shootaround, to lock in on execution. Now he has a coach who’s as good as there is at execution.” It feels like Rivers may have been taking some shots at Antetokounmpo, but if this is something he told him while coaching him, it could be fine.

item.title: A viewer's guide to the NASCAR Chase finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway: Five storylines to watch on NBC
item.description: Homestead-Miami Speedway has always been a happy place for Kyle Larson, but he should feel a new level of joy Sunday at the 1.5-mile oval in South Florida. With a 67-point lead on Christopher Bell, Larson is a 99.4% favorite (per Racing Insights analytics) to clinch his second consecutive NASCAR Cup Series championship and third overall in the 2026 season finale. He needs only nine points over 400 miles at Homestead, which means he could clinch the title if he's in the top three when Stage 1 ends on the 80th lap Sunday. That almost seems a foregone conclusion for Larson, who has won two of the past four Cup races at Homestead (including the most recent in March 2025) and has never scored fewer than 18 points in 12 starts there. How to watch 2026 NASCAR Chase finale at Homestead-Miami: TV info, schedule, entry list, Cup points standings The season will conclude at the 1.5-mile oval in South Florida. Nate Ryan , Few drivers were more enthused than the Hendrick Motorsports star about the Chase finale returning to Homestead after a six-year run at Phoenix Raceway — where Larson won titles in 2021 and last season but has also struggled on the flat 1-mile oval. His aggressive style is a better fit on the 1.5-mile high banks at Homestead, which was the ending point of the Cup schedule from 2002-19. Its history is nearly as appealing as its wide, sweeping surface that allows for multiple lanes of racing. "It's a great track in an amazing part of the country," Larson said. "Yeah, the championship weekend was held here for so long. Even before I raced here, I always looked forward to championship weekend. There's been a lot of cool moments from this place. "Then getting to race here, this track is awesome too. Definitely was a different feel whenever it wasn't championship weekend, so I'm glad it's back and we can all have some fun." Here are other storylines to watch Sunday (with the prerace show beginning on NBC at 2 p.m. ET and the race starting shortly after 3 p.m.): High line to glory Running well at Homestead comes with the risk of putting a car inches from the wall at 200 mph every lap. That's where Larson, the dirt track veteran who has made a career of running "the cushion" on the high side of racetracks around the country, is most comfortable, and he won't be changing that despite the stakes Sunday. "Although it doesn't look like it because I run so close to the wall, I'm always trying to get to the end of the race," he said. "That's the main objective. So I would say there's no difference in that for me. The most grip is against the wall, so usually where the most grip is is a little bit easier." Though a slip of the wheel can damage the car, Larson said the consequecnes have been lessened since the 2022 introduction of the Next Gen model, which is more durable. "With the old previous car, most of the grip is still at the top, but there's way more risk up there," he said. "Now there's still risk, but a lot less. I foresee my race looking like an

item.title: Exeter City defender James agrees new deal to 2028
item.description: Ed James first joined Exeter's academy as an eight-year-old [Shutterstock] Exeter City defender Ed James has signed a new contract to keep him at St James Park until the summer of 2028. The League Two side also has an option to extend the 21-year-old Wales Under-21 international's deal by a further 12 months. The centre-back has played 23 times in all competitions for the Grecians since making his debut in October 2022. He has become an important first team player this season, staring half of their League Two fixtures. The academy graduate has been with Exeter since he was eight and has also had loan spells at Yeovil Town and Torquay United. "Since I've come back to the club, Ed has been excellent," manager Matt Taylor told the club website. "He's a young player with huge potential. He's got great size, moves quickly for a centre-half and is aggressive. There's a lot to like about him. "He's still developing, both physically and in his understanding of the game, but he's performed well this season. He's another young player we want to build the future around. "It's another signal of our trust in the youth policy and shows the importance of the academy. "You can have all the taglines you want about developing young players, but the proof is in the pudding. You have to play them, invest in them and give them time. That's what a contract is for. "It's pleasing that some of these young players are now wanting to commit to us. I think they can see the opportunity here, and that will hopefully filter down throughout the academy." All the latest Exeter City news

item.title: James out for minimum of five games - Bompastor
item.description: James was substituted in the 6-0 win at Charlton last weekend [Getty Images] Chelsea manager Sonia Bompastor says Lauren James will be out for at least the next few weeks, casting doubt on her availability for England's World Cup qualifying play-off matches. The 25-year-old will miss at least the next five matches for the Blues, including Everton's visit to Stamford Bridge on Saturday and a crucial match against champions Manchester City next weekend. It also casts doubt on her chances of being available for England's World Cup qualifying play-off matches against Ukraine in December. After James came off in distress in the 35th minute of the 6-0 win over Charlton Athletic, Bompastor confirmed the injury: "The only one who will be missing is LJ. "She had a scan and she has an injury in her hamstring, so we won't see her until the end of this block." There was more positive news for Chelsea, with midfielder Lexi Potter, who made her England debut last month, back after missing the trip to Charlton. Chelsea, meanwhile, are top of the WSL table having won matches both with and without James this season. Bompastor added: "Of course we know how good Lauren is for us and for the team. "Also, my job is to make sure I find solutions when some players are not available and not playing for the team. I think the good thing is that when I looked at some of the statistics from last week, we are a team who are able to score through different players. "The last game we had against Charlton, a lot of players were involved in scoring again. Also, I think every player on the pitch had a shot on goal. "Even if it was not always a great one, at least all of the players who were on the pitch had a shot on goal. I think that's a good thing and, again, my job now is to make sure I find the solutions without LJ on the pitch." Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

item.title: Panthers sign ex-Eagles, Raiders cornerback before Week 9 game vs. Broncos
item.description: Panthers sign ex-Eagles, Raiders cornerback before Week 9 game vs. Broncos originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Carolina Panthers are sitting atop the NFC South heading into Week 9, but there is some real concern about this team with a 3-4 record following two brutal losses. They lost 43-13 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and then 27-19 to the Green Bay Packers . While their run defense struggled against the Buccaneers, their pass defense couldn't stop the Packers in Week 8. To try to fix things on the back end of the defense, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Panthers are signing 26-year-old cornerback Jakorian Bennett to the practice squad. Panthers sign Jakorian Bennett to bolster CB depth "The Panthers signed former Raiders and Eagles CB Jakorian Bennett to the practice squad," Rapoport reported. This isn't a massive move for the Panthers, but considering the team's shaky defensive back depth, Bennett might get real playing time in the not-too-distant future. Will Lee III, Mike Jackson, Akayleb Evans, and Jaycee Horn are all hurt right now. Only Lee has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Broncos . If Lee can't go, the Panthers will be down to relying on Malcolm DeWalt IV a lot, as the rest of their CB depth chart is banged up. Bennett might see a role right away as the Panthers' CB room is dealing with a lot of injury issues. MORE : Jerry Jones defends Brian Schottenheimer after Cowboys collapse vs. Cardinals Bennett is 26 years old and has played in 35 games across three seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders and Philadelphia Eagles. He has 12 passes defended with 65 total tackles in his career to go with a solid 81.5 passer rating allowed. Across the 2025 and 2024 seasons, he's allowed a 66.5 and 67.7 passer rating, respectively. He hasn't played in 2026 as he's dealt with an injury issue, but now with the Panthers, he might be good to go. Carolina needs all the help they can get on defense, as their CB room is very depleted by injuries. Bennett might play a big role in Week 9, as the Panthers' cornerback injuries are reaching a breaking point. item.title: Bo Naylor Reveals He Didn't Know Depths of MLB Gambling
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers catcher Bo Naylor If any MLB players didn't believe that allegedly fixing games came with serious consequences, the images from the federal trial involving Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz this week should have changed their minds. Clase and Ortiz were in New York on Thursday to face conspiracy charges for allegedly fixing individual pitches for prop bets during the 2025 season. Catcher Bo Naylor, who was a teammate of both pitchers with the Cleveland Guardians at the time, testified that he "didn't know" individual pitches could even be bet on. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! "I didn't know that before," Naylor said, according to The Associated Press. "I didn't know that until (this) situation." Prosecutors expressed disbelief that Naylor could be unaware of the nature of such bets, according to the AP report, and showed video of multiple pitches that have been called into question. Naylor was called upon to testify because, as a catcher, he would have been involved in game-planning and calling pitches for Clase and Ortiz, and might have known if they didn't throw the pitches he'd called. When pitches missed the strike zone -- in some cases, spiked into the dirt or airmailed to the backstop -- Naylor testified that he simply chalked it up to even the best pitchers often missing their spots. Naylor appeared in 207 games as a catcher over the 2024-2025 seasons with Cleveland. He was limited to 27 total games with the Guardians this season before he was traded to the Milwaukee Brewers, with whom he played only three games. He did not appear in a postseason game for the eventual World Series champions. More MLB: Cubs Should Steer Clear of Signing Tarik Skubal

item.title: F1 Brazilian GP: Lando Norris tops FP1 as Colton Herta clinches superlicence
item.description: Motorsport photo Lando Norris was fastest in Free Practice 1 at Formula 1’s Brazilian Grand Prix, leading Kimi Antonelli, Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton. Norris outpaced Antonelli by 0.082s on the soft rubber with a time of 1m11.717s, while Verstappen and Hamilton were two and three tenths adrift respectively, with the top-four teams again all close together. Not all of them were happy, however, with Verstappen complaining over team radio about a long-time problem of the RB22: “Unacceptable, man. Unacceptable, these downshifts. What the ****?” Later on, he mentioned yet another issue: “There’s something wrong with my steering. It’s getting harder and harder to turn the wheel.” There were hefty lock-ups galore in Turn 1 for veterans and rookies alike – and there were many of the latter in action. The most prominent of them undoubtedly was Rafael Camara, with Haas’ 2027 driver making an early F1 debut at home this weekend following Esteban Ocon’s fallout with the team. Formula 2’s championship leader was 18th-fastest in this session, nearly nine tenths slower than team-mate Oliver Bearman. One rookie who did outpace the sister car was Alpine’s Gabriele Mini, who took seventh place with a 1m12.569s, 0.085s quicker than Franco Colapinto. No other rookie run driver made it into the top 10; McLaren’s Leonardo Fornaroli was 11th (+1.116s vs Norris), Williams’ Luke Browning 17th (+0.080s vs Alex Albon, who had a mechanical problem) and Cadillac’s Colton Herta 20th (+0.904s vs Valtteri Bottas). Gabriele Mini, Alpine F1 Gabriele Mini, Alpine F1 Herta’s trouble-free session – other than a mammoth lock-up into Turn 1 – should theoretically mean he will collect the final required point for an FIA superlicence, making him eligible to a 2027 F1 seat should Cadillac elect to promote him next year. Ferrari’s Dino Beganovic and Audi’s Freddie Slater propped up the classification after encountering technical issue which prevented them from setting soft-tyre times and restricted their mileage. “The car has just switched off,” Slater said, causing a red flag just 12 minutes into the session. The pair completed 11 and seven laps respectively. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Kellymoss returns to IMSA WeatherTech championship full-time in 2027
item.description: Motorsport photo Longtime Porsche customer team Kellymoss will return to full-time IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship competition in 2027. Michael Clark will make his IMSA debut in the Grand Touring Daytona (GTD) class in the #17 Porsche 911 GT3 R (992), partnering with Colin Braun for the full season. Kyle Marcelli joins for the IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup rounds, with a fourth driver for the Rolex 24 At Daytona to be named later. Kellymoss last raced full-time in the WeatherTech Championship in 2023 under the Kelly-Moss with Riley name, winning the GTD class at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca. As part of its continued collaboration with Riley, the team is moving its operations from Wisconsin to North Carolina. “We're excited to return to the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship with Michael and Colin,” said Andy Kilcoyne, Team Principal and co-owner. “Having won both sprint and endurance championships with Michael in 2024, it's been rewarding to see his continued development and the partnership he's built with Colin since we brought them together in late 2025. This is a significant step forward for everyone involved, and we're focused on building a program capable of competing at the front.” Clark steps up to GTD following a season racing a Porsche GT3 car with Braun. “I'm incredibly excited and privileged to be competing in the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship in 2027,” Clark said. “Colin and I have been working hard to prepare both the car and myself for this next step. Competing at this level is a dream come true, and I'm grateful to Kellymoss, Colin and IMSA for the trust and confidence they've placed in me. I can't wait to get started.” Braun brings 174 IMSA starts, 26 wins, and three series championships (2014, 2015 PC, 2022 LMP3) to the program, along with prior GTD experience in a Porsche in 2017. “I'm incredibly excited for 2027,” Braun said. “Michael and I clicked right away as co-drivers and built a great friendship throughout the 2026 season. Being part of his first full-season IMSA program is something I'm really looking forward to. He's put in a tremendous amount of work to prepare for this next step, and with the support of Kellymoss behind us, I believe we'll be well positioned to deliver strong results throughout the year. We're putting together a great group of people who are motivated to succeed, and we're going to have a lot of fun along the way!” Marcelli, who has GTD and PC wins, returns to IMSA grid action after competing in Lamborghini Super Trofeo North America in 2026. “I'm excited to join Kellymoss, Colin and Michael for the 2027 IMSA WeatherTech Championship,” Marcelli said. "There are so many great ingredients coming together in this program. Kellymoss has a rich history of success with Porsche and has assembled an experienced and talented group of people. It's an honor to join this organization. “Colin and I have raced against each other for much of the past 15 years, and I've always had tremendous r

item.title: I’ll sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight – Tinubu
item.description: By Nwafor Sunday President Bola Tinubu has said he will spend the night in Akwa Ibom State, declaring that his visit is a “second term presidential sleep” as he expressed confidence in securing re-election in 2027. Tinubu made the remark on Friday during a reception and rally organised in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo. Addressing the crowd, the President thanked the people of Akwa Ibom for their support and urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 general election. “Thank you, Akwa Ibom. I love you with my heart. I will sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight. It’s going to be a second term presidential sleep. I will dream of victory too. “I will depend on you to go out and vote. The weapon you have is the PVC. If you have not collected it, please go ahead and collect your PVC. I am begging you, for the sake of your future,” he said. Tinubu also reiterated his administration’s promises of improved living conditions, infrastructure development, education, skills acquisition and job creation. “I promised you a better future, I promised you development, I promised you education. I promised you skill development, I promised you jobs. We are going to plant a lot of economic trees,” he added. The President’s declaration comes amid criticism from the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, who had taken a swipe at him over his travels across the country. Obi had suggested that Tinubu had not spent the night in any state outside Abuja and Lagos, a remark that appeared to question the President’s physical presence across the country. Tinubu’s announcement that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom comes against the backdrop of the exchange between the two political figures as political activities ahead of the 2027 general election gather momentum. The post I’ll sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight – Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Vikings’ Star O-Lineman Unsure on Status vs Bills
item.description: Photo courtesy of the Minnesota Vikings Carson Wentz will start in place of Kyler Murray (hamstring) this week at quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings, on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. Both teams hold a 6-1 record, but the Bills come in as -3 road favorites. What happens at quarterback beyond Week 9 is anyone’s guess. If Wentz plays well, it will be difficult to replace him with Kyler Murray, who has been one of the worst QBs in the NFL this season, through six starts. But Murray might not be the only starter missing on offense for the Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium. In total, nine Vikings landed on Thursday’s injury report , and seven of them were limited in practice. Minnesota Vikings left tackle Christian Darrisaw dealing with a shoulder injury The most concerning one might be on the far left side of the offensive line. In the Vikings’ last loss to the Lions, Christian Darrisaw injured his shoulder. When he met with reporters at his locker on Thursday, the star offensive linemen didn’t seem confident that his shoulder is going to be ready for Monday night’s game. The transcript is below but it doesn’t do the video justice. It’s Darrisaw’s body and tone that seem most doubtful. Doesn’t sound encouraging based on this answer from Christian Darrisaw about his shoulder. He was a limited participant in practice yesterday, but seems like that shoulder could be a problem: pic.x.com/1d3YvgMmkz — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) November 6, 2026 Reporter: “Are you pretty sure the shoulder’s okay?” Darrisaw: “We’re taking it a day at a time.” Reporter: “Encouraging though, that you were out there today?” Darrisaw: “Absolutely, absolutely.” Reporter: “Was there some fear immediately after the game Sunday, were you thinking, ‘Uh-oh, maybe it could be something severe’?” Darrisaw: “Never fear. Um, I know I trust this training staff. Um, at the end of the day, it just come down just to being smart and um, just listening to what, what they’re saying and and telling ’em, give ’em good feedback on how my body’s feeling. And uh, when Monday gets here, we’ll, we’ll, we’ll see.” Christian Darrisaw – KSTP Related: Report: Vikings in Market for QB at Trade Deadline It’s the second injury Darrisaw has dealt with this season. He entered concussion protocol after the Dolphins game and missed Week 5 at New Orleans. He has started six games this year. Christian Darrisaw not sure yet about playing the Bills It has also been two years since he tore his ACL and MCL in Week 8 of the 2024 season at the Rams. He had surgery two years ago nearly to this day (Nov. 4, 2024). The injury came just three months after he signed a four-year extension worth $77 million guaranteed. Whoever starts at left tackle will be tasked with protecting Carson Wentz’ blindside, where he will work plenty against Greg Rousseau, who leads Buffalo with seven sacks . item.title: Official: Paul Nebel extends contract with Mainz 05
item.description: Official: Paul Nebel extends contract with Mainz 05 As officially announced by the Bundesliga club this afternoon, Paul Nebel has extended his contract with 1. FSV Mainz 05. The midfielder, who joined the club at Bruchweg as a 13-year-old, progressed through all the youth teams at Mainz's academy. Nebel has worn the 05ers' jersey for over ten years, with the exception of a two-year loan spell at second division side Karlsruher SC. Still only 24 years of age, Nebel has already made 95 appearances in all competitions for Mainz, providing 15 goals and 18 assists. “Paul is the prime example of how a player from our own youth academy can develop into a very important player for our Bundesliga team. “He has shown a lot of passion, patience and a down-to-earth attitude,” explained Mainz sporting director Niko Bungert. "Paul is an important and reliable pillar for our team and someone who has shown in recent years that he is always there when needed. "We are happy that we have found a very good solution for our future together with him.”

item.title: Tigers could pursue another Yankees All-Star 2B after Gleyber Torres
item.description: Tigers could pursue another Yankees All-Star 2B after Gleyber Torres originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Tigers could be looking for a new second baseman during this offseason. Gleyber Torres is a free agent after spending the past two seasons with the Tigers, hitting .260/.364/.363 with eight home runs and a 105 OPS+ in 96 games in 2026. Torres has become a great on-base guy the last few years, but he offers little to no value with his legs on the basepaths. Detroit could have Zach McKinstry and Hao-Yu Lee split time at second base, or they could target another former New York Yankees middle infielder. "The lineup is less of a concern, but Jazz Chisholm Jr. to Detroit wouldn't be a colossal surprise. "At any rate, the last time the Yankees let a multiple-time All-Star second baseman walk in free agency without even extending him a qualifying offer, Gleyber Torres ended up with the Tigers. Perhaps they bring in Chisholm to replace him," Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller wrote. Chisholm doesn't get on base nearly enough to match Torres' .364 OBP, but he hit 19 homers and stole a career-high 41 bases this past season. The Tigers stole 58 bases across 162 games, just 17 more than Chisholm swiped by himself. MORE : Phillies predicted to sign Cubs' $85M former Silver Slugger finalist Adding athleticism to the lineup could help the Tigers get back to the top of the AL Central. Obviously, Chisholm's been a topic of discussion for some negative reasons, including playing the field with a lollipop in his mouth. You'd like to think the Tigers would make it clear that those kinds of things are not allowed, especially under manager A.J. Hinch. They could use a few additions to the starting rotation too, but signing Chisholm would be a solid start to the offseason for Detroit. item.title: Arizona’s Tommy Lloyd takes laundry list of learning lessons from first win of season vs. Cal Poly
item.description: Eakin Howard-Imagn Images Arizona’s Tommy Lloyd takes laundry list of learning lessons from first win of season vs. Cal Poly appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After falling to UCLA in the season opener, Tommy Lloyd and the No. 5 Arizona Wildcats got their first win of the season with a 104-84 beatdown of Cal Poly at home. Motiejus Krivas, who returned to Arizona amid NBA buzz , led the Wildcats with 30 points and eight rebounds. During his post-game interview with Andy Katz, Lloyd shared what he was most satisfied with in win No. 1. “Getting the win’s nice. We’re obviously a team that’s figuring itself out. Cal Poly, give them a ton of credit. They played so hard and just kept coming. We had some really good moments. Hopefully we could build on it. We had some moments when we kind of let up a little bit. You can’t let up at this level. Our team has to establish the effort we need to play with all the time. So it’s a little bit of a work in progress,” Lloyd said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) And when asked what he wanted to build on, the reigning Naismith Coach of the Year winner got on his team for failing to rebound and being “allergic” to loose balls. While Lloyd wasn’t pleased with the team’s rebounding, the Wildcats still had a 44-30 edge on the boards. The Euro frontcourt of Krivas and Ivan Kharchenkov led the way with 18 rebounds combined, while backup big man Evan Otten added seven boards in just nine minutes. One area that Arizona will need to get better at is 3-point shooting. They went just 4-of-14 from beyond the arc after going a mere 7-of-30 in the loss against UCLA. Lloyd and the Wildcats will look to improve on that and their ability to get to loose balls in their next game against Northern Arizona on Tuesday.
